resources.string: Keep your place on both devices
NeoSync carries your reading position between Neo Reader on this Boox and CrossPoint on your Picco.
You read here in Neo Reader. NeoSync notices each page turn and saves your position online.
On the Picco, open the same book and choose Sync Progress. It jumps to where you stopped.
It works the other way too: read on the Picco, and Neo Reader opens at the new place.
Accurate to about a page. Your notes and highlights stay in Neo Reader; only the position is synced.
The firmware the Picco ships with has no progress sync. You first need to install CrossPoint, a free open-source firmware, on the Picco.
On a computer, open crosspointreader.com and follow the instructions for the Boox Picco.
The Picco is flashed over USB. It takes a few minutes.

Before you flash: Boox does not support custom firmware and says installing it may void your warranty. Some units may be locked. This is your decision; NeoSync is not affiliated with Boox or CrossPoint.
Turn on sync on the Picco
On the Picco, open Settings → Connectivity → CrossPoint Sync.
Leave the server address empty. That uses CrossPoint’s free sync server, the same one NeoSync uses.
Choose Sign Up to create your account, or create it here in NeoSync in a moment. Use the same username and password on both devices.
Sync Behavior: “Smart sync” decides by itself which device is ahead. “Ask every time” lets you pick Apply Remote or Upload Local.
To sync on the Picco: open the book, press Confirm, then choose Sync Progress.
NeoSync recognises a book by its file name. Put the same EPUB on both devices, with exactly the same file name.
Copy the file to both devices without renaming it. A renamed copy is treated as a different book.
Use EPUB files. Positions in EPUBs are matched by chapter and are the most accurate.
Before fetching a position from the Picco, close the book in Neo Reader. A book that is open on screen can’t be moved.
Let NeoSync work in the background
NeoSync needs two permissions, and Boox needs to be told not to stop it.
Used to read each book’s chapter list, so positions are exact.
A small permanent notification keeps sync running.
If the NeoSync icon is greyed out, long-press it and choose Unfreeze.
In Settings → Apps → NeoSync, allow it to run in the background and to start automatically.
Use the same account as on your Picco. No account yet? Choose a username and password and tap Create account.
Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
Enter a username and a password.
That username is already taken. Try Sign in, or pick another name.
Could not reach the sync server. Check Wi-Fi and try again.
Your password is never stored on this device, only a scrambled form of it. Your reading positions are kept on the sync server below.
Leave empty for CrossPoint’s server. Any KOReader-compatible sync server works; it must be the same on the Picco.
Nothing synced yet. Read a few pages in Neo Reader.
Sync is running in the background.
Syncs your position in the background
Automatic sync is off. Nothing is sent until you turn it on; the buttons below still work.
Sync normally happens by itself. Use these buttons to force a direction. Close the book in Neo Reader before using “Fetch from Picco”.
No book with a reading position yet. Open one in Neo Reader first.
Online: nothing saved for this book yet
Position fetched. Open the book in Neo Reader.
Set the Picco address in Settings → Connection first.
The tablet isn’t connected to the Picco’s network. Connect it to the Picco’s hotspot — or put both devices on the same Wi-Fi — then try again.
Book sent. It appears in the Picco’s library.
Already on the Picco — nothing to send.
Can’t reach the Picco at %1$s. Check the address in Settings → Connection and make sure the Picco’s File Transfer screen is open.
Something went wrong talking to the Picco: %1$s
The sync server address must start with https:// — your account details would otherwise travel unencrypted.
Can’t read the book file. Allow book file access via “How it works”.
192.168.1.50 — shown on the Picco’s File Transfer screen
Set the Picco address in Settings to see its books here.
Asking the Picco for its library…
Not listed yet. Open File Transfer on the Picco, then tap refresh.
No books on the Picco yet.
No books to sync: none of the Picco’s books has been opened on this Boox.
Positions synced: %1$d fetched, %2$d sent, %3$d already up to date.
It looks like you’re on the Picco’s hotspot, which has no internet. Switch back to your usual Wi-Fi to sync positions. Sending book files works here.
It looks like you’re on the Picco’s hotspot. Switch back to your usual Wi-Fi to sync positions.

Can’t reach the sync server: this Wi-Fi has no internet. The Boox is probably on the Picco’s hotspot, which only works for sending book files. Switch back to your usual Wi-Fi to sync positions — or have the Picco join that Wi-Fi (File Transfer → Join a Network) so both work at once.
Can’t reach the sync server. Check the internet connection, then try again.
Comparing this Boox’s books with the Picco’s…
Every EPUB on this Boox is already on the Picco.
%1$d EPUB books on this Boox aren’t on the Picco yet (%2$s in total). They go into “%3$s”. Keep the Picco’s File Transfer screen open while they are sent.

Copies a short report (device model, firmware, NeoSync’s recent log) to paste where you report the problem: a Reddit comment or message, or a GitHub issue. Book names, file paths and your account details are removed. Nothing is sent by the app.
